clue.text: Shame one went round street party

indicators.note: the shame word and the 'one' letter are said to go round the street abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: fie is an old exclamation of disgust, as in 'fie for shame'
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed slips round the block during a neighbourhood street party.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive celebration of the Spanish kind, so it is a party.

clue.text: He does not trade in local goods

definitions.text: He does not trade in local goods

parts.words: He does not trade in local goods
parts.note: a merchant who deals in goods brought from abroad rather than home-made ones; the clue is framed as if describing a shopper who buys elsewhere

explanation.definitionFit: A trader who brings goods in from overseas deals in foreign rather than local produce.

clue.text: Time-server's punishment?

parts.note: a time-server here is literally a prisoner serving time, and what a court hands down to that person is the penalty

explanation.walkthrough: A 'time-server' usually means a lazy employee coasting along; here it is a prisoner doing time.
explanation.definitionFit: A court's penalty handed to a convict is a term or verdict, the punishment a prisoner serves.

clue.text: Yearn for ideas to be bounced round next

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed round the yearning word, enclosing it
ideas bounced about get thrown around, so the letters of ideas are mixed up

parts.note: to yearn for something is to long for it

explanation.surface: Someone longs to have their ideas batted around in a brainstorm that comes next.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram ASIDE, made by 'to be bounced', is split by 'round' so its first letter sits before the yearning word and the rest after; 'for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed beside another thing is next to it, side by side.

clue.text: A baby might be — protesting strongly

definitions.meaning: an infant is often carried cradled in someone's embrace
being furiously indignant about something, as an idiom for outrage

explanation.definitionFit: A baby is often held in a parent's embrace, and the same idiom means being angrily indignant.

clue.text: X, an unpredictable person

definitions.meaning: in algebra x stands for a value not yet found
someone whose behaviour nobody can forecast

explanation.definitionFit: In algebra x is the variable whose value is not given; figuratively the phrase describes someone whose behaviour cannot be forecast.

clue.text: Normal tone

definitions.meaning: in music a note that is neither sharp nor flat

explanation.definitionFit: Something natural is ordinary or unforced; in music a natural is a note neither sharpened nor flattened.

clue.text: Reserved model has little money about at first

annotationWithheld.why: Reserved model has little money about at first (8): RE (about) first + CENT (little money) leaves TI, which 'model' does not give by any standard reading (Model T gives only T); no parse found
annotationWithheld.clue: Reserved model has little money about at first

clue.text: Crumpets cooked in a range of colour!

indicators.note: food that is cooked has been worked on and changed, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Toasted crumpets come out in a whole palette of browns.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is the band of hues white light splits into, from red to violet.

clue.text: Spread out art production — one can find holes in it

definitions.text: one can find holes in it

parts.note: laid flat and unfolded means open
a piece of art produced is a work

explanation.surface: A sprawling art piece is so full of gaps that critics pick holes in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Openwork is lace, metal or woodwork patterned with gaps through it, so it is full of holes by design.

clue.text: Body height not right in representation

indicators.note: not having the right letter means that letter is taken away

parts.note: a person's stature is how tall the body is

explanation.surface: A sculptor's portrayal gets the figure's height wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a carved or cast figure depicting a person, a likeness in stone or bronze.

clue.text: Encourage ten, it appears, playing rap first, to play in quick succession

indicators.note: the jumbled rap letters are placed at the front of the answer
rap being played about suggests its letters are moved around

parts.note: to egg someone on is to encourage them
the figures of ten, 10, look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A rapper is urged on with ten seconds to deliver the lines quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges RAP into ARP, which 'first' puts at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: An arpeggio is a chord whose notes are sounded one after another in quick order rather than together.

clue.text: Reported attempt by firm treating first fabric

indicators.note: said out loud, so a word that sounds like the attempt word is wanted

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: only the opening letter of treating is used

explanation.surface: A company reportedly tries treating a new textile first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tricot is a knitted cloth, a fine warp-knit material used in clothing.

clue.text: I'll enact movement of customers

indicators.note: the letters of the words are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone vows to stage a campaign to bring in shoppers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliental is an adjective meaning relating to clients, the people a business serves.

clue.text: Existing during an expectant time

parts.note: an expectant time is pregnancy, so this means occurring in the months before birth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Expectant' sounds like mere waiting, but here it means expecting a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Antenatal means before birth, the stage of pregnancy when a mother is expecting.

clue.text: An expression of agreement. Honest!

definitions.meaning: a word said to concur with someone, like 'quite so'
sincere, genuine, said as an assurance

explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'quite right' signals agreement, and someone sincere and straight is faithful and accurate.

clue.text: He'll dart off despite being enslaved

indicators.note: something gone off has turned bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A captive dashes off despite being held in bondage.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in thrall is to be in bondage, so someone thralled is held as a serf.

clue.text: Rocky, one from France stayed round

parts.note: un is French for one

indicators.note: the letters of stayed are turned round into another order

explanation.surface: A Frenchman stayed around somewhere shaky.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky in the sense of wobbly or likely to topple describes something not firm on its feet.

clue.text: Very small part, it's half the alphabet

definitions.meaning: the first half of the letters runs from A to M

explanation.definitionFit: An atom is a tiny particle; read as 'A to M' it covers thirteen of the twenty-six letters.

clue.text: Next to a disc-jockey, one not lacking heart

parts.note: DJ is the standard abbreviation for disc jockey
an ace is the one in a deck of cards

indicators.note: only the outside letters of not are kept, its middle letter gone

explanation.surface: Beside a DJ stands someone who is not short of courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjacent describes things lying beside each other, neighbouring.

clue.text: Charge too much?

parts.note: read not as overpricing but as loading or filling something past its capacity

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge too much' suggests overpricing; charge here means load, as with a glass or a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a container is to fill it, so filling beyond capacity is charging it too much.

clue.text: Paid back although wholly in debt

indicators.note: the wholly word is set inside the debt word

parts.note: being in the red means being in debt
quite means wholly or completely

explanation.surface: A loan was repaid even though the borrower is deep in debt.
explanation.definitionFit: Love that is requited is returned in kind, so the feeling has been repaid.

clue.text: Rex is to come up to the dish

parts.note: R stands for rex, Latin for king

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, so the word to is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The king is to come up to the table for his meal.
explanation.walkthrough: R for Rex (king) appears on coins and in 'ER'.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian rice dish cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Certify that testimony — part thereof

indicators.note: only a part of the words that testimony is taken, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A notary vouches for a witness statement, or at least a section of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness, to confirm formally as genuine.

clue.text: Type of food on dray in new form

indicators.note: the letters are given a fresh shape, a different arrangement

explanation.surface: Food delivered on a brewer's cart arrives in a novel guise.
explanation.walkthrough: A dray is a low cart used by brewers to deliver barrels.
explanation.definitionFit: Food free of milk and its products, such as vegan cheese, is labelled this way.

clue.text: Favour hut

definitions.meaning: to incline towards or prefer something
a simple shed propped against a wall

explanation.definitionFit: To incline towards something is to prefer it; a lean-to is a shed with a sloping roof built against a wall.

clue.text: I printed version undaunted

indicators.note: a new version of the words is a different arrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper's printed edition remains fearless.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless, brave in the face of danger.

clue.text: Routine every 24 hours

definitions.meaning: ordinary, everyday, as in mundane tasks
happening daily, one cycle each sunrise

explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary chores are everyday matters, and something occurring daily recurs in this fashion.

clue.text: Not much like bo-peep

definitions.meaning: the nursery-rhyme shepherdess is called ... Bo-Peep

explanation.definitionFit: A small amount is not much; the nursery rhyme's shepherdess who lost her sheep bears this word in her name.
